review.title: notFound() never reaches the wire: dead addresses answer 200
review.notes: IMPLEMENTED IN THE TREE AND NEVER CLAIMED, like the rest of recovery packet 1 -- but PARTIALLY, and the two gaps are different in kind. This is the fifth task found in that state, and its code landed while it sat BACKLOG and unowned: control/events.jsonl records apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx and page.tsx being edited as belonging to PL-0704 while it was blocked on a lifecycle dependency. So it must be started with --reconcile-existing, never against HEAD. IT IS A MODIFICATION TASK IN THE REVIEWER'S TAXONOMY, MOSTLY, and that changes the probe. Its central act was a DELETION -- the root loading.tsx removed -- and marker absence cannot witness a deletion. What it also did, and what CAN be witnessed, is introduce two named components where anonymous route-level skeletons used to be: CatalogSkeleton in app/page.tsx and PlaybackLoading in app/watch/[contentId]/page.tsx, each now a Suspense fallback sitting BELOW the existence decision rather than a loading file wrapping the whole segment. Those two names are new even though their markup is not, so a pickaxe on the names finds the relocation, which is precisely this task's work. Use them as the witnesses; do not use the deleted file. TWO GAPS AGAINST THE ACCEPTANCE, AND ONLY ONE IS A CODE GAP. FIRST, THE TITLE SKELETON, WHICH I BELIEVE IS A CONTRACT GAP RATHER THAN A DEFECT AND AM FLAGGING FOR A RULING RATHER THAN FIXING. The acceptance says any fix must KEEP the loading skeletons rather than deleting them to move a status code. Home and watch comply: both relocated their skeleton into a Suspense boundary below a cheap existence check that consults nobody. The title route did not -- it deleted its skeleton outright -- and its own header argues why: on that route a status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before the catalog answers whether the title exists, which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect the task exists to remove. The only honest way to restore one would be a section whose data does not depend on the title existing, and none exists today. So the code looks right and the clause looks over-general. I am not rewriting the acceptance to match the code unasked -- that is the move the reviewer has twice had to authorise explicitly, on PL-0205's wording and on PL-0706's -- so it is proposed here and left for the verdict. SECOND, THE PRODUCTION-MODE 404, WHICH IS NOT THIS TASK'S TO CLOSE. An unknown title answers 404 under development and 200 with a refusal panel under production, and that is correct rather than broken: on a hosted build no catalog metadata source is constructible, so loadTitleDetail reports error rather than not-found, notFound() is unreachable, and a build that answered 404 there would be claiming an absence it never looked for. The precondition is a catalog source that exists in a deployment, which is PL-0305's, now READY since PL-0105 completed. ALLOWEDPATHS CORRECTED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS. apps/web/src/app/(home)/** is DROPPED: it is a dead declaration for a route-group approach that was considered and rejected, it reserves a directory that does not exist, and it starves nothing only by accident. apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx is KEPT even though the file is deleted, because the deletion is the change and a surface that omitted it would not fingerprint the task's central act. TWO PATHS ADDED. docs/E2E.md, because it and .github/workflows/ci.yml currently CONTRADICT EACH OTHER about whether the two 404 assertions have ever been observed passing -- E2E.md claims an executed 2026-09-05 pass on all four browser projects, ci.yml says UNKNOWN, expected to pass, never observed passing -- and settling that is exactly what this task's EXECUTED clause is about. It is declared by PL-0706, which is DONE, and by PL-0703, which is BLOCKED, so no active conflict. And .github/workflows/ci.yml, which UNTIL NOW WAS DECLARED BY NO TASK IN THE REPOSITORY AT ALL: every CI change this project has made has landed outside every declared surface. That is a real declaration hole rather than a convenience, and this task adopting it is a partial fix at best -- the file is repository governance rather than frontend, and it should eventually belong to whatever task adopts CLAUDE.md and control/README.md, which are undeclared for the same reason.
review.acceptance: An unknown title id and a malformed watch id each answer HTTP 404 rather than a skeleton served at 200, proven by an EXECUTED Playwright run ON THE PINNED BROWSER REVISION rather than by a route calling notFound(), and rather than by a run on a substituted revision. The cause is that a segment's loading file wraps that segment in Suspense, so React flushes the shell at 200 before the access-fallback error escapes the render and Next can set the status; the root loading file wraps every route in the application, so per-route fixes alone are insufficient. THE SKELETON CLAUSE, AMENDED. Any fix must RELOCATE the loading skeletons below the existence decision rather than deleting them to move a status code, ON EVERY ROUTE WHERE A SECTION'S DATA DOES NOT DEPEND ON THE ADDRESS EXISTING. The title route is exempt, and the exemption is reasoned rather than granted: a well-formed unknown title id is indistinguishable from a real one until the catalog answers, the status line precedes the first body byte, so no byte may be sent before that load resolves -- which is the definition of having nothing to stream. A full-page skeleton there IS the defect this task exists to remove, so the unamended clause required the defect on one of the three routes it governs. The exemption is EMPIRICAL AND REVERSIBLE, not permanent: the moment the title page grows a section whose data does not depend on the title existing -- recommendations, continue-watching, anything PL-0301 or PL-0501 fetches separately -- it gains an in-page Suspense below the decision exactly as the watch route has, and this clause binds again. Home and watch satisfy it today and a positive check proves each, because the original wording was satisfied by a repository with no skeletons in it at all: every assertion was a not.toContain on a string that exists nowhere. DEPENDS ON PL-0103 because the title route is that task's declared write surface; this is a lifecycle dependency, not a technical one.

HOW THE REVISION WAS PROVEN RATHER THAN ASSUMED, because 'it ran' is exactly what the shim round could also have said: playwright install --dry-run under the same environment prints the install location as /root/.cache/ms-playwright/chromium_headless_shell-1234, while under the ambient environment it prints /opt/pw-browsers/chromium-1234, a path that does not exist -- so a run with PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH left in place would have FAILED to find an executable rather than quietly using 1194; DEBUG=pw:browser logged exactly one launch path, the 1234 headless shell; and the two binaries were asked their versions directly. THE RUNS, at integrated head e097590ee79e112f26073b293a4ad7fbb2bd1fd6, from e2e/ after npm ci there: development, LIBERTY_E2E_WEB_MODE=development npx playwright test --project=api --project=chromium, exit 0, 43 passed 3 skipped 0 failed; production, the default, same projects, exit 0, 34 passed 12 skipped 0 failed. Asserted statuses unchanged from the shim run: /title/no-such-title-pl0701 is 404 under development and 200 with catalog_source_not_configured under production; /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id is 404 in BOTH modes; / and /watch/<demo id> are 200 WITH their skeleton strings present; and /title/<demo id> is 200 with NO 'Loading title', which is the positive form of the exemption's premise and is new this round, because a not.toContain on an unknown id cannot distinguish 'refused before any byte' from 'this string is nowhere in the repository'. Second witness: the dev server's own log recorded GET /title/no-such-title-pl0701 404 and GET /watch/Not%20A%20Valid%20Id 404. BEHAVIOURAL DIFFERENCE FROM 1194: NONE -- same counts, same skips, same statuses, no new flake -- and that is reported as a finding rather than as reassurance, because a newer Chromium could legitimately have changed Suspense flush behaviour, which is why the revision is pinned at all. WHAT THIS IS STILL NOT: it is two projects, not the device matrix -- WebKit, mobile-safari and Firefox were not launched, so PL-0705's WebKit clause is untouched -- it is one run per mode with retries 0, and it is NOT the CI job. No claim is made that the CI job will be green: a container run is a different machine, a different install path, a warm turbo cache and CI unset, so reuseExistingServer was on and forbidOnly off. The CI workflow as configured would install the pinned revision from the lockfile-pinned @playwright/test with no version literal, and run the same two projects -- but no run of it has ever been observed.

review.title: Macrolanguage and extlang equivalence in the shared language matcher
review.notes: THE REVIEWER'S OWN CARVE-OUT FROM THE PL-0203 APPROVAL, not a finding of this lane's. gpt-architect approved PL-0203's script/trim corrective and, in the same verdict, identified this as a genuinely separate defect and agreed it should be its own cross-lane media task covering both audio and subtitles. In substance: the zh-yue / zh-cmn instinct points at it, but it is not a script issue -- those are Cantonese and Mandarin extended-language/macrolanguage distinctions; RFC 5646 specifically notes that the Chinese languages encompassed by zh are generally not mutually intelligible when spoken, so a matcher that collapses both to primary zh can call the wrong SPOKEN language a preferred-language fallback. The reviewer proposed P0 and stated explicitly that this does not invalidate the script/trim corrective PL-0203 landed. IT IS DISTINCT FROM THAT SCRIPT RULE, and the distinction is the whole task: a script subtag identifies a WRITING SYSTEM, which is why require_compatible_script is right for automatic subtitle selection and deliberately looser for audio; this is about MUTUAL INTELLIGIBILITY OF SPEECH, an audio-first fact that reaches subtitles only because both surfaces share one matcher. It depends on PL-0203 rather than racing it because it corrects the same function -- languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts, which subtitles.ts imports -- and two concurrent owners of that function would collide. Provenance of the verdict is the same as PL-0203's review record: transcribed by Claude from the ChatGPT review session rather than received over the agent bus. IMPLEMENTED IN ROUND 45, AND IT IS THE ONLY TASK IN THE RECOVERY CAMPAIGN THAT NEEDED NO PROVENANCE WORK AT ALL -- genuinely unstarted, so an ordinary start captures a true base. THE RULE IS STRUCTURAL, WITH NO REGISTRY VENDORED, exactly as the script rule already is. A new spokenLanguage helper answers which language will come out of the speakers rather than which subtag a string starts with, and it differs from primarySubtag in precisely one place: where a macrolanguage has been narrowed by an extended-language subtag. BCP-47 spells a language as 2*3ALPHA optionally followed by an extlang of exactly 3ALPHA, while a region is two letters or three DIGITS and a script is four letters, so three ASCII letters immediately after a two- or three-letter primary is unambiguously an extlang and nothing else can take that shape in that position. RFC 5646 permanently invalidates the second and third extlang positions, so there is at most one to find. THE COLLAPSE RUNS TOWARD THE SPECIFIC RATHER THAN THE GENERAL, which is what makes the equivalence clause work in both directions: zh-cmn becomes cmn rather than zh, so the prefixed and bare spellings of one language agree, and the equivalence survives any region or script suffix because those subtags are never consulted. A bare zh stays zh -- it names the macrolanguage and neither variety, so treating it as either would invent a preference the viewer did not express, which is the same asymmetry the script rule uses when it says a tag naming no script conflicts with nothing. THE NEW OUTCOME IS ITS OWN REASON, as the acceptance requires: preferred_language_other_variety_only, distinct from preferred_language_other_script_only and from the regional fallback, because the three have different remedies -- a script conflict is about READING and the dialogue is still the viewer's, a regional difference is cosmetic and is still selected, and this one is the wrong language. Reporting it as a regional fallback would move the defect out of the matcher and into the vocabulary. ONE THING WORTH KNOWING THAT THE DESIGN MADE TRUE BY ACCIDENT AND THE TESTS NOW PIN: the script and variety findings are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE rather than merely ordered. matchesOnlyAcrossScripts requires a match under ignore_script, setting the script aside leaves the spoken-language comparison, and a different variety fails it -- so zh-yue-Hant against a zh-cmn-Hans preference is not across both boundaries, it is simply the wrong language and the script question is moot. Only a track in the viewer's own spoken language can be across the script boundary, which is the only case where a font is the remedy. EXERCISED THROUGH BOTH CONSUMERS, which the acceptance demands because the two share one comparator precisely so they cannot drift, and the way that guarantee fails is one being corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. selectAudioTrack is asserted not to hand a Mandarin listener a six-channel Cantonese track that would have won on quality had the language matched, and selectSubtitleTrack is asserted to refuse a Cantonese subtitle under the new reason while still returning it in ordered for a player to offer. TWO PROPERTIES HAD TO BE TIGHTENED RATHER THAN MERELY KEPT PASSING, and that is the most useful thing this task turned up. Both audio.property.test.ts and subtitles.property.test.ts asserted that a matched pair shares a PRIMARY SUBTAG, which was a restatement of the rule being removed; once zh-cmn and cmn are both in languageTagArb it is simply false, since that is one spoken language with two primary subtags. Both now ask spokenLanguage, which is the stronger claim and the one the matcher actually makes. The arbitrary gained zh, zh-cmn, zh-yue, cmn and yue-hk so the property suites reach the new path at all -- without that they would have kept passing while testing nothing about it. ALLOWEDPATHS NARROWED BEFORE THIS TASK IS EVER CLAIMED, for the reason recorded on PL-0204: packages/contracts/** prefix-contains PL-0706's leaf packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts, so the wildcard would hold this P0 behind an unrelated security corrective for no benefit. The three contracts entries are where the language vocabulary this task corrects actually lives -- domains/subtitles.ts carries the subtitle policy and its outcome vocabulary, domains/audio.ts the track contract, and testing/arbitraries.ts the language-tag generators the property suites draw from. Narrowed on a PREDICTION rather than on a diff, unlike PL-0204's and PL-0205's, because this task is not yet written: if the correction turns out to want a new shared leaf -- a language-tag vocabulary of its own, say -- that is a deliberate widening at claim time with a line in this field, which is the ordinary path and is cheaper than a wildcard that reserves a whole package. packages/media-engine/** stays wide: this task owns the matcher and both its consumers, and it shares an owner with PL-0204 and PL-0205.
review.acceptance: The shared languageMatch in packages/media-engine/src/audio.ts stops reducing a tag to its primary subtag where that reduction crosses a MACROLANGUAGE boundary. A spoken-language distinction encompassed by a macrolanguage is not reported as a preferred-language fallback: zh-yue against zh-cmn, and either against a bare zh preference, must not answer with a fallback strength, because a fallback there tells the caller it may play Cantonese for a Mandarin preference. Canonical primary and extlang spellings of the SAME language are treated as equivalent in both directions -- cmn and zh-cmn are one language, yue and zh-yue are one language -- and the equivalence survives a region or script suffix on either side. The rule is exercised through BOTH consumers of the shared matcher, the audio track selection in audio.ts and the subtitle selection policy in subtitles.ts, rather than through the helper alone, so neither consumer can be corrected while the other keeps the old behaviour. Any new outcome carries its own named reason: a distinction that is not regional must not be reported with a regional-fallback reason.

review.title: Corrective, re-run: auth integration decision, with a forgeable profile scope and an unsupported pin
review.description: This task SUPERSEDES PL-0401. It carries three merits blockers as well as a provenance correction, and the merits are the larger half. PROVENANCE: PL-0401 recorded implementationBaseSha fc1ea4d54c9e7d2b2f6d9aa71a977abdc3bcb400, proven with ENABLED_AUTH_CAPABILITIES and WITHHELD_AUTH_PLUGIN_FAMILIES. Those witnesses correctly located the code introduction and missed earlier task implementation on another declared write path: docs/DATA_MODEL.md did not exist at 56b343 and was created in bbe68ed8, before the recorded base, already identifying itself as covering this task's auth boundary and already selecting Better Auth 1.7.1. The true lower bound is 56b3435418f222f557ce957e7d5de3827da107b7 while docs/DATA_MODEL.md remains a write surface. PL-0401 is BLOCKED with the false range preserved as audit history. DO NOT CLAIM THIS TASK UNTIL THE THREE BLOCKERS IN THE NOTES ARE IMPLEMENTED; it is created now so the findings are recorded against a task rather than living only in a review transcript.
review.notes: BLOCKER 1, AND IT IS THE PL-0706 DEFECT IN A SECOND PLACE. ProfileScope carries a type-only unique symbol property while mintProfileScope returns an ordinary object via cast, so a caller holding a genuine scope can write a spread with a replacement profileId and TypeScript carries the branded structural type straight through -- without the explicit cast ADR-007 claims is the only forgery route. Downstream persistence then trusts scope.profileId directly, which makes this a cross-profile data-access bypass rather than a typing nicety. The prescription: make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability rather than a compile-time proof, use issuance identity as well. The pattern already exists in this repository twice -- ClassifiedRuntime in packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts and PinnedTarget in media-inspection -- module-private brand, freeze, WeakSet registry, identity check as the consumer's first action. THE SURFACE THIS IMPLIES IS WIDER THAN THIS TASK CURRENTLY DECLARES, AND THAT IS SETTLED BEFORE THE CLAIM RATHER THAN DISCOVERED DURING IT. The reviewer offered two levels: at minimum make the scope genuinely nominal so a spread copy cannot remain assignable, and if it is meant to be a runtime capability, use issuance identity as well. The minimum is NOT ACHIEVABLE IN THE TYPE SYSTEM, and PL-0706 already established why: a spread copies a branded property along with everything else and type-checks with no cast at all, so only object identity rejects it. TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable. Therefore the runtime registry is not the optional upper level here, it is the only level that works -- and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ASK. The consumers are in another package: packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts and watchlist-repository.ts read scope.profileId straight into their predicates, and profile-repository.ts and repository-scoping.test.ts also handle the type. So this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration, and it will then overlap PL-0402, PL-0403 and PL-0404, which are BACKLOG today and must be sequenced after it. The alternative -- brand and registry in packages/auth with no consumer asking -- would produce a capability that looks unforgeable and is not, which is worse than the present state because it would read as fixed. Whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason. BLOCKER 2, AND THE EXACT PIN IS WORKING RATHER THAN FAILING. better-auth and its Drizzle adapter are pinned at exactly 1.7.1. Upstream's current release is 1.7.4, from 2026-09-10, and its security policy supports only the latest version. The reviewer was explicit that this is not an argument against exact pins: it proves the policy works by making staleness visible, which is what ADR-007 said it was for. Move both packages together and update REVIEWED_BETTER_AUTH_VERSION. DO NOT BUMP AND LEAVE THE MIGRATION: 1.7.3 restored the 1.6 account core schema after the issuer-schema change in 1.7.0 through 1.7.2, while this repository's hand-written migration still has an issuer column and an (issuer, account_id) uniqueness rule. The migration must be regenerated or reconciled against the reviewed version BEFORE security approval. That is why packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql moves from reviewDependency to WRITE PATH here: on PL-0401 it was only evidence, and read-only was correct; here it has to change, and reviewDependencies are read-only by contract. PL-0402 also owns packages/persistence and is BACKLOG, so no active conflict exists today, but the two must be sequenced and the reviewer should say which owns that file afterwards. BLOCKER 3. ADR-007 still states obsolete control-plane routing, naming gpt-architect as preferred implementer and claude-lead as reviewer, while the record now correctly has claude-backend implementing and gpt-architect reviewing independently. Rewrite that paragraph as history rather than as current routing, and prefer wording that points at the task gate as authoritative -- otherwise completing the review needs a post-approval edit that immediately stales the fingerprint it just bound. TWO HONEST CAVEATS CARRIED FORWARD FROM PL-0401, neither an unmet clause: the migration has never been executed, because no PostgreSQL exists in this environment, and better-auth.ts is deliberately untested. SEQUENCING: this task is READY rather than BLOCKED because nothing external gates it, but it should not be claimed until the three blockers are implemented, and claiming it early would reserve packages/auth and two documents while no work was happening.
review.surfaceWidenedAtClaim: WIDENED 2026-09-15 by claude-lead in the same edit that claimed the task, which is what the notes instruct: 'this task must declare packages/persistence/src/** as a write path when it is claimed, not merely the migration' and 'whoever claims this should widen the declaration in the same edit that claims it, and say so in the reason'. TWO ENTRIES WERE ADDED, AND THEY ARE NOT THE SAME KIND OF ADDITION. First, packages/persistence/src/**, exactly as prescribed: the registry is the only mechanism that rejects a spread forgery, TypeScript cannot make a spread unassignable, and a registry closes nothing unless the consumers ask, so the consumers must change. This was demonstrated rather than argued: with the issuance check in place and persistence untouched, packages/persistence/src/repository-scoping.test.ts fails six tests, because its fixtures build scopes with 'as unknown as ProfileScope' and refuseForeignScope now refuses them. progress-repository.ts moves from reviewDependency to write path for the same reason and is removed from reviewDependencies rather than listed twice. Second, package-lock.json, WHICH THE REVIEWER DID NOT NAME AND WHICH IS THEREFORE FLAGGED FOR THE REVIEWER RATHER THAN PRESENTED AS PRESCRIBED. The notes require better-auth and its Drizzle adapter to move together; the root lockfile still resolves 1.7.1, so after the pin moves, npm ci refuses the mismatch and every gate that starts from a clean install fails before it runs. Leaving it stale would ship a dependency bump that cannot be installed reproducibly, so the lockfile is part of moving the packages rather than a separate concern. It is a generated file owned by no active task; PL-0001, which generated it, is DONE. If the reviewer would rather see it as its own task, it is one entry to remove. NO OTHER WRITE SURFACE WAS ADDED, and packages/persistence/src/schema/auth.ts is inside the prescribed entry rather than an extra: it still declares the issuer column and the (issuer, account_id) unique that the migration reconciliation removes, so leaving it would make drizzle-kit propose reinstating both on the next generate. REVIEWDEPENDENCIES ALSO CHANGED, AND IT IS A REPLACEMENT RATHER THAN A WIDENING OF WRITE ACCESS. packages/persistence/src/progress-repository.ts left the list because it became a write path and listing it in both would say two different things about the same file. In its place the two files the reviewer named as the pattern this implementation must copy are declared read-only: packages/contracts/src/shared/runtime.ts (ClassifiedRuntime) and packages/media-inspection/src/pin.ts (PinnedTarget). Neither is written; they are declared so the approval fingerprints the originals against which the copy is judged, which is exactly what reviewDependencies is for. If the reviewer considers that padding, they are two entries to remove and nothing else changes. SECOND WIDENING 2026-09-15, ROUND 43, BY COMMANDER INSTRUCTION AND WITH THE SAME DISCLOSURE. apps/web/src/lib/db/** was added so the in-memory repository can be converted. The first round named it as the one remaining hole and stated its bound precisely rather than reassuringly: createInMemoryRepository refuses to construct without an issued ClassifiedRuntime, so it cannot exist in a deployment -- a development- and test-process bypass, not a production one -- and it is still a cross-profile bypass, because fourteen call sites read input.scope.profileId off the object instead of asking the registry. A registry that half the repositories ask is a capability that reads as unforgeable and is not, which is the failure mode this whole corrective exists to remove, so leaving it would have been the PL-0706 defect in a THIRD place. The commander ruled on 2026-09-15 that all profile ids must flow through the same validated accessor as the production repositories. CONFLICT CHECKED IN BOTH DIRECTIONS BEFORE ADDING: the prefix apps/web/src/lib/db is disjoint from PL-0704's apps/web/src/app/loading.tsx, apps/web/src/app/page.tsx, apps/web/src/app/title and apps/web/src/app/watch, which are the only other active apps/web declarations; PL-0701's apps/web/** would contain it, but PL-0701 is BACKLOG and unowned. Removing profileId from the ProfileScope interface entirely -- the change that turns an unchecked read from a deprecation into a compile error -- becomes reachable once this conversion lands, and whether to take it is flagged for the reviewer rather than assumed.
review.acceptance: A recorded decision selects the auth approach and states the boundary it implies: a packages/auth seam the rest of the application depends on instead of the vendor library, database-backed sessions, a deliberately small enabled surface with the advanced plugin stacks left off, and an exact-pinned dependency whose upgrades are treated as security-sensitive work rather than floated on a caret range. The pinned version must be one upstream currently supports, and the hand-written migration must agree with that version's account schema rather than an abandoned intermediate one. ProfileScope must be UNFORGEABLE by a holder of a genuine scope: a spread copy carrying a replaced profileId must not remain assignable, and any consumer that grants data access on the strength of a scope must establish that the scope was ISSUED rather than merely that it type-checks. The decision record must describe the routing that actually applies, or point at the task record as authoritative rather than restating it.

A ROUND-42 CORRECTION THAT BELONGS IN THE RECORD RATHER THAN IN A CHANGELOG: this round's first typecheck in the working worktree returned exit 0 as a TURBO CACHE HIT, 9 of 9 cached in 95ms, over a tree where packages/*/node_modules were absent and better-auth did not resolve at all. Forced, the same tree exited 2 with 'Cannot find module better-auth' plus roughly forty TS2532 in the web app. The dependency linkage was repaired and every figure quoted in this round's evidence is from a --force run. That is exactly why this project forces rather than caches, and it is reported because an exit code that was observed is evidence even when it is superseded.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force at integrated head e097590ee79e112f26073b293a4ad7fbb2bd1fd6, exit 0, 15 of 15 tasks and 0 cached, 2112 passed 1 skipped 0 failed -- up from 2096 at round 42. THE HOLE ROUND 42 NAMED IS CLOSED. apps/web/src/lib/db/in-memory-repository.ts read input.scope.profileId in fourteen places and was a cross-profile bypass in every development and test process; all fourteen are gone, seven scope-taking methods now bind profileIdFromScope as their FIRST statement ahead of content-id and limit parsing so a forged scope cannot use a validation reason code as an oracle, and selectActiveProfile keeps the one documented exception it shares with persistence, establishing issuance through scopeBelongsToSession before the account match and refusing with a mapped reason rather than a throw. AND THE PROPERTY CAME OFF THE TYPE. profileId and grantedFor moved to a module-private IssuedProfileScope; the public ProfileScope carries only the brand, which turns every future unchecked read from a deprecation into a compile error. The removal produced exactly the compile errors that prove it bites -- 3, 4, 16, 6 and 5 across five suites -- each converted to the accessor rather than cast away. THE LIMIT IS STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: it does not make forgery impossible. Object.assign({}, real, {profileId: victim}) was verified under tsc --strict to type as ProfileScope with NO CAST ANYWHERE, so both forgery suites were rewritten to that spelling and the runtime registry remains the only control. New apps/web/src/lib/db/scope-forgery.test.ts, 13 cases, store behind a Proxy that throws on any property access so refused and refused-before-touching-storage are distinguished, exhaustiveness MACHINE-CHECKED by partitioning the adapter's members and asserting the partition equals Object.keys, and one case runs a genuine scope through to the store, because a refusal suite passes just as happily against a repository that refuses everything.

integration.evidence: THE MIGRATION WAS EXECUTED, NOT RECONCILED. PostgreSQL 16.15 (Ubuntu 16.15-0ubuntu0.24.04.1), cluster 16/main, installed and started in this container; a dedicated role and database were created rather than using the superuser. psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f packages/persistence/migrations/0000_profile_scoped_identity.sql exit 0, 8 CREATE TABLE and 7 CREATE INDEX; re-applied to a second empty database, exit 0, 8 tables, 20 indexes, 26 constraints, proving the file is clean from empty rather than only from the state the first run left. THE GENERATOR WAS RUN, AND THE COMMAND THIS REPOSITORY TOLD READERS TO RUN IS THE WRONG ONE. @better-auth/cli is deprecated on npm, latest 1.4.21, and depends on better-auth 1.4.21 directly, so npx @better-auth/cli generate would have described a version this repository does not use. The version-matched CLI is the npm package 'auth': auth@1.7.5 pins better-auth 1.7.5 and @better-auth/core 1.7.5 exactly. npx auth@1.7.5 generate against the real createLibertyAuth config, exit 0, 'Schema was generated successfully!'. THE DIFF, FIELD BY FIELD against information_schema on the applied database: no missing column, no extra column, no type mismatch, no nullability mismatch across user, session, account and verification; every index and unique the library asks for exists physically. All three round-42 changes confirmed -- the issuer column is absent from the generated schema, the library declares NO unique index on account at all, and the (provider_id, account_id) unique is therefore OURS rather than upstream's, which round 42 claimed and this round proves. Its safety argument was executed rather than argued: a deliberate duplicate was refused with 23505 on account_provider_id_account_id_key. The profile half was exercised in SQL: the display-name unique, the cross-household selection refusal, both progress check constraints, a NULL-position lease, and the delete cascade. NO CHANGE TO THE MIGRATION WAS REQUIRED. THREE THINGS THIS DOES NOT PROVE, STATED SO THE GATE IS NOT READ AS MORE THAN IT IS: drizzle-kit is still unrun and migrations/meta carries no journal or snapshot, so the file is applied by psql rather than by the tool that owns it; concurrency was never raced, so the guarded writer-epoch UPDATE was executed as a statement and not contended, and postgres-repository.ts has still executed nothing; and a naive mechanical diff reports 36 false findings because the expected schema keys fields camelCase while the physical columns are snake_case -- the clean diff quoted here maps expected fields through the Drizzle schema to physical names, and a reviewer re-running the naive comparison should know why it disagrees. review.title: Supersession is a field, and a task cannot stay gated behind one
review.description: Four tasks -- PL-0205, PL-0401, PL-0601, PL-0703 -- are BLOCKED, terminal, and superseded by a corrective re-run. Each says so only in prose. BLOCKED transitions only to BACKLOG, READY or CANCELED, so a superseded task can never reach DONE, and with completion.requireAllDependenciesDone true, any task depending on one is gated forever. That is not a hypothetical: PL-0301 was gated behind PL-0205 while PL-0207 sat DONE, and with it PL-0302, PL-0501, PL-0502, PL-0701 and PL-0702. A human noticed. Nothing in ai:validate could have.
review.notes: SCOPE IS THE VALIDATOR, NOT A DEPENDENCY REWRITER. The rule reports; it never edits a dependency, because repointing a dependency is a task-definition change and those are deliberate, reasoned and recorded -- see PL-0301's own notes for what that looks like. An automatic repointer would make the graph self-modifying on the strength of a field any writer can set. THE RULE, PRECISELY. For each task T declaring supersededBy S: S must exist, must not be T, and T must not itself be DONE, or that is an ERROR, because a DONE task that claims to be superseded is two contradictory records of the same work. If S declares supersedes, it must name T -- a one-way pointer is a typo waiting to be trusted. Then, for each task D whose dependencies contain T: if S is DONE, ERROR, because D is gated behind a task that can never complete while its replacement already has; if S is not DONE, WARN, because the edge is not yet fatal but will become so the moment S completes, and a warning that arrives before the deadlock is the entire point. WHY ERROR AND NOT WARN FOR THE FIRST CASE. ai:validate already treats provenance drift as a warning and structural impossibility as an error. A dependency that can never be satisfied is structural: no sequence of legal transitions resolves it. It belongs with 'missing dependency' and 'invalid status', not with drift. WHAT THIS RULE CANNOT DO, STATED SO NOBODY OVERTRUSTS IT. supersededBy is self-asserted, exactly like fromAgent on the agent bus. It proves that somebody wrote a pointer, not that the successor genuinely carries the predecessor's work. A wrong pointer produces a wrong error or hides a real deadlock. It is a cheap alarm on a failure mode that has already cost this project one stalled milestone, not a proof of anything.
review.acceptance: ai:validate refuses a task graph in which a task depends on a task that declares supersededBy and whose named successor is DONE, and warns when the successor is not yet DONE. It also refuses a supersededBy naming a missing task, naming itself, declared on a DONE task, or contradicted by the successor's supersedes field. The rule reports and never edits a dependency. The four existing supersession pairs validate clean, and a regression in scripts/test-ai-control-plane.mjs proves the rule fires -- both that it errors on a reconstructed PL-0301-behind-PL-0205 graph and that it stays silent on the repaired one, so it cannot pass by being inert.

review.title: Windows desktop shell and the PlayerAdapter boundary
review.description: Project Liberty's first production target is Windows desktop on the commander's own machine. The commander has settled the direction: a Tauri shell, the existing Next.js application preserved rather than rewritten and served by a Next standalone sidecar, a PlayerAdapter boundary the application and domain layers depend on instead of any concrete player, libmpv for compatible non-DRM playback, Shaka/EME retained for DRM-capable playback, capability routing made explicit before playback rather than discovered during it, and an LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline of our own rather than a GPL prebuilt. This task records that decision and specifies the boundary. It writes documentation only -- no shell, no adapter, no dependency is added here, because the instruction is that architecture is recorded before a large irreversible implementation, not after it.
review.notes: THE AUDIT CAME FIRST AND IT FOUND A CLEAN SLATE. A repository-wide search for electron, tauri, mpv, libmpv, webview2, neutralino and nw.js across every .ts, .tsx, .json, .md, .mjs and .yml outside node_modules returned nothing. So neither shell was favoured by anything already in the tree, and the decision was made on evidence rather than on inertia. Today's player is shaka-player ~5.2.6 with xstate ^5.32.5 and custom-media-element in apps/web. THE DECIDING FACT IS COMPOSITING, NOT BUNDLE SIZE. Putting HTML chrome over a hardware-accelerated native video surface in one window on Windows is a documented, shipping arrangement on WebView2 -- ICoreWebView2Controller2::put_DefaultBackgroundColor accepts alpha 0 or 255 only, and at 0 the host's content renders beneath -- and has no supported path on Chromium, where PPAPI is gone and child HWNDs are no longer in the window hierarchy. Stremio ships the WebView2 plus libmpv --wid arrangement in production on Windows and measured its previous render-API-into-a-texture approach as 2-5x worse. Any size-based argument for Tauri should be dropped: with a Node sidecar the installer lands near Electron's anyway. THE SIDECAR IS WHAT PRESERVES THE APPLICATION. Tauri's default is a static export, which would force every /api/v1 route handler off Next -- a rewrite of the application's architecture, which the instruction forbids. output: standalone in a sidecar keeps Server Components, route handlers, proxy.ts, cookies(), headers(), Server Actions and ISR working. It costs a Node runtime in the bundle, a loopback listener, supervision code and Tauri's CSP injection, which does not reach an external http origin. ONE QUESTION THIS TASK DOES NOT DECIDE AND MUST NOT DECIDE SILENTLY. A sidecar runs the application's server on a machine the user administers. If provider resolution runs there, then the boundary that enforces invariants 1 and 2 executes from files the user can read and replace, with whatever credentials it needs in its environment. The alternative is that the desktop build implements those specific routes as an authenticated proxy to the backend -- same route, same contract, same URL, a different implementation behind it, selected by build target, which is ordinary adapter work rather than a rewrite. This document states the question, states the recommendation, and leaves the ruling to the reviewer and the commander. It is a design input to PL-0501 and is cheaper to supply now than to retrofit. DRM IS A ROUTING CONSTRAINT, NOT A GAP TO CLOSE. mpv has no CDM and cannot be given one. That is not something to work around: the mpv adapter must REFUSE a DRM-protected candidate with a named reason and must never attempt it, never fall back and never degrade. Which means capability routing has to be an explicit, reasoned decision before playback -- canPlay returning a reason on both branches -- rather than a guess discovered at load time. That is what makes invariant 2 structural here rather than a promise, and it is why the boundary carries a capability descriptor at all. THE LICENSING WORK IS THE LONG POLE AND IT GATES SHIPPING RATHER THAN PROTOTYPING. A stock prebuilt libmpv is a GPL build and must not ship in a closed-source product; the one LGPL variant on offer statically links an LGPLv3 FFmpeg and carries its builder's own no-warranty disclaimer. Building our own with -Dgpl=false and an LGPL FFmpeg, with an SBOM, converts an open-ended exposure into a reviewable artifact. Nothing in this document is legal advice and counsel review is named as a precondition of shipping rather than assumed.
review.acceptance: A recorded architecture decision states the Windows desktop target, the Tauri shell, the preserved Next.js application served by a standalone sidecar, and the LGPL-compatible libmpv/FFmpeg build pipeline, each with the evidence it rests on and the strongest argument against it. It specifies PlayerAdapter as an interface the application and domain layers depend on -- load an authorized playback session, play, pause, seek, stop, select audio track, select subtitle track, set volume, expose position and duration, expose buffering and stall events, expose recoverable and fatal errors, expose track metadata, expose A/V sync telemetry where available, dispose -- with no mpv, Electron, Tauri or Shaka type reachable from it, and names the two implementations behind it and the explicit capability routing that chooses between them, including the requirement that the mpv adapter refuse DRM-protected candidates with a named reason rather than attempt them. It states that media addresses continue to come only from authorized provider resolution and the playback-session boundary and that the client can never submit one, that stream candidate ranking stays in @liberty/media-engine, and that provider-specific logic stays in @liberty/provider-sdk. It states where provider resolution runs in the desktop build as an open question with a recommendation rather than deciding it silently, because that answer is a design input to PL-0501. It records what was verified, what was not, and which specific facts would reverse each decision. No shell, adapter or dependency is implemented here.

recommended.title: Contract module boundaries
recommended.acceptance: Shared vocabularies live in their own leaf modules, domain contracts live in one module each, index.ts is a re-export-only compatibility barrel rather than the authoritative public surface, and a wildcard exports map lets a new domain contract be added without touching package metadata or the barrel; no cycle-driven z.lazy remains and structural regressions prove the boundary rather than merely reflecting it; no schema behaviour changes

recommended.title: GitHub bridge for cross-agent review
recommended.acceptance: GitHub becomes the shared state bridge for Claude Desktop and OpenAI review without manual file copying

recommended.title: A real catalog metadata source
recommended.notes: The discovery layer has no metadata source. PL-0105 landed a seam, and docs/CATALOG_SOURCE.md says so in its first line; this task is the thing that belongs behind it, tracked so the gap stays visible instead of being hidden by a port that looks finished. docs/PRODUCT_SPEC.md step 2 of the initial user journey is browse/search normalized metadata, and nothing in this repository ingests any: every surface reads six fictional works. PL-0301 and PL-0302 do not close it - they supply stream candidates, which is what a title plays from, not what a catalog is made of. PARTLY BLOCKED, and the split is deliberate rather than a hedge. The design half - identity and dedupe, refresh and staleness, tombstones, paging, provider-side search, the locale-tagged contract, and the undeclared-rights state that catalogItemSchema cannot currently express - needs no external access and can begin now. Connecting an actual metadata provider, and carrying artwork, cannot: both need an agreement and credentials, which control/policies.json escalates to human-only under Licensing and Credentials - the same categories that block PL-0302. It is a DIFFERENT agreement from PL-0302's, covering catalog metadata and image rights rather than stream rights, so this is not merely waiting on that task; the honest status is BACKLOG with the ceiling named, not BLOCKED on someone else's licence.
recommended.acceptance: A metadata source stands behind resolveCatalogMetadataSource and answers what the port deliberately does not. Ingestion: something fetches, schedules and backfills, rather than an array being maintained by hand. Refresh: an answer carries its age and a stated staleness policy, so nobody has to guess how old a rail is. Identity and dedupe: how a provider's native id becomes a normalizedContentId, and what happens when two sources describe the same work, is settled as a design decision before it is coded - this is the largest missing piece and it is not a coding question. Deletion: a work that disappears from a source produces a tombstone, so it stays distinguishable from a fetch that failed. Paging and provider-side search: listRecords returning everything is a shape only six fixtures can use, and who owns ranking and paging is part of the contract rather than an accident of in-memory filtering. Artwork: images arrive with their own licensing, tracked separately from the work's, or they do not arrive. Localization and availability: title, genre and synopsis are locale-tagged and a work can be offered in more than one language, and availability windows and territory exist, so the empty state's claim about a region is backed by something. Every record declares a rights basis whose category agrees with its item and whose reference is an opaque internal identifier or null, and the ingestion path is treated as untrusted third-party I/O - allowlisted egress, bounded bodies, redirects revalidated, and no media address anywhere in a catalog payload.
